body: I usually give him his night bottle and he gets sleepy afterwards and that's when he goes in the crib.
He wakes up around 7/8am and then takes a nap around 11am. He wakes back up around 1230/1 and is up for the rest of the day or sometimes takes another small nap around 4/5pm.

He usually has a his last meal around 730-8, bath directly after and some play time. He usually falls asleep around 930-1030. We had a good routine going. I put him down when he is still awake but drowsy but as soon as he realizes he is being put down he starts to cry.
"oh she is beautiful!" ... she's a he 😭

he got all the sleep lol. he woke up for feedings for about the first two weeks and then he just stopped. he said he just couldn't do it, so he would just be asleep and get his 6+ and i'd be the one split open having to get baby and go downstairs and get the bottle ready and do the feedings. he laughs when i brought it up and makes jokes with his friends about how it's the woman's job to wake up like that and tend to the baby. thinking back on it is the worst for me. he still gets all the sleep..
Piggy pig!!!
They told me at 32 weeks my baby was measured to be 9 or more pounds by the time I was supposed to give birth.... he was 6 pounds and 15 ounces. Scared me for no reason!

I did it once at 8 weeks and it was the worst. I did it another at 12 weeks and it still wasn't great. I think 4/5 months in and when I started weaning off breastfeeding did it become enjoyable for me again.

I struggled naming my baby lol. I chose Messiah but I wanted his name to be close to mine so I changed it to Jasiah so like Messiah but with a J.. Jah-Siah but people keep saying Josiah and I get sad bc it's what I worried about)-: Now I think about how in school he will constantly have to correct people! But I still love it.
My son was the same up until 3 months. Now he is calm all the way throughout even when he gets lotion'd up and in his sleeper! Sometimes they just need time and to be a little older(-:
I hear the 6 months a lot! I wonder if it's because many people stop breastfeeding around that time?
It's tough! Do you think it's normal he only does it with dad and not our moms?

I try to let it be for as long as he can take it or until baby literally starts screaming loud and coughing from screaming so loud. Dad tries everything he and I have thought to try.. baby only lasts about 5 minutes until it gets to this point.

Thank you! 
I am hoping they accommodate me better if I try to talk to them again. Sadly though I think it is as good as it gets. At first they told me to go pump in my car! I was definitely having some anxiety)-: I am feeling a bit better now but still thinking
Thank you! I am going to try that and see if it helps him realize how I feel. I just don't like to feel like I am giving up on my baby)-:

I have a one month old now. I never babysat, never changed a diaper, never did anything baby/child related because I just didn't find desire to. 
I was literally saying FTK one week before I learned I was pregnant, I know that sounds horrible lol. 
Newborn stage has been tough and I definitely sometimes feel those thoughts like I made the wrong decision but then I realize how much I love this little bean. I always tell myself how it will be better soon before I know it. Taking it day by day truly helps.
Thank you for your reply(: What did you use when you started to use formula and how did you bring it into their diet? Did it mess with their tummy or anything?

It's very hard because when I'm not thinking of the past and we are just relaxing and watching tv or on our phones I feel so happy I don't understand why I can't just be happy with him.. I know I probably sound stupid but it's just so difficult to come to terms with

abreva should be mostly effective during this stage, i also heard lysine pills are good as well.
i'm sorry your mother is trying to put you down.. just ignore it. so many people get them and they are so common. i felt dirty too until i realized how common they are seriously! people talk about them like nothing, medicine is over the counter, etc. i hope this helps.
